To execute the film’s jaw-dropping “garbage truck” dress reveal, Academy Award-winning costume designer Jenny Beavan constructed a staggering 40-foot train from 393 distinct pieces of upcycled clothing. The physical garment was so massive and heavy that Emma Stone could not actually walk or move while wearing it. Instead, she had to be securely anchored to the back of the moving truck while the production crew meticulously packed and folded the colossal train around her. Because the sheer weight of the practical fabric made it physically impossible to capture the entire sequence in motion practically, the VFX team seamlessly blended Beavan’s physical creation with digital extensions to show the dress violently cascading down the street, perfectly marrying old-school practical fashion design with modern visual effects.
Cruella (2021), directed by Craig Gillespie, starring Emma Stone, Emma Thompson, Joel Fry. Set in 1970s London amidst the punk rock revolution, a brilliant but rebellious young grifter named Estella embraces her wicked, chaotic alter ego to exact revenge on the ruthless fashion legend who destroyed her family.

source_details.synopsis: Cruella is a 2021 American crime comedy film directed by Craig Gillespie from a screenplay by Dana Fox and Tony McNamara, and a story by Aline Brosh McKenna, Kelly Marcel, and Steve Zissis. Produced by Walt Disney Pictures, Marc Platt Productions, and Gunn Films, it is based on Dodie Smith's 1956 novel The Hundred and One Dalmatians, serving as a backstory for its antagonist, Cruella de Vil. It is also the third live-action adaptation in the 101 Dalmatians franchise. The film stars Emma Stone as the title character, with Emma Thompson, Joel Fry, Paul Walter Hauser, Emily Beecham, Kirby Howell-Baptiste, and Mark Strong in supporting roles.
